## Result

**Answer: ML Canvas (higher share, first) and BDD scenarios (absolute minimum, second) are the two least-used requirements-documentation formats in ML-enabled system projects.**

### D1. Final ranked table — primary base: 194 respondents who answered Q10
`used` ≡ value `quoted`; `-77` = item non-response → respondent excluded (sentinel NA, never a zero). Bootstrap = respondent rows resampled with replacement, B=10,000, seed 20261025; percentile CI is headline, Wilson and basic shown for robustness.

| rank (asc) | format | k | % | Wilson 95% | percentile 95% | basic 95% |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **BDD Scenarios** | 4 | **2.062** | 0.805–5.181 | **0.515–4.124** | 0.000–3.608 |
| 2 | **ML Canvas** | 15 | **7.732** | 4.741–12.364 | **4.124–11.856** | 3.608–11.340 |
| (tie) | Others *(residual, excluded from ranking)* | 15 | 7.732 | 4.741–12.364 | 4.124–11.856 | 3.608–11.340 |
| 3 | Vision Document | 29 | 14.948 | 10.614–20.644 | 9.794–20.103 | 9.794–20.103 |
| 3 | Goal Models | 29 | 14.948 | 10.614–20.644 | 10.309–20.103 | 9.794–19.588 |
| (opt) | Not Documented *(response option, excluded)* | 30 | 15.464 | 11.052–21.217 | 10.825–20.619 | 10.309–20.103 |
| 5 | Data Models | 34 | 17.526 | 12.821–23.491 | 12.371–23.196 | 11.856–22.680 |
| 6 | Use Case Models | 38 | 19.588 | 14.616–25.740 | 13.918–25.258 | 13.918–25.258 |
| 7 | Prototypes | 42 | 21.649 | 16.435–27.965 | 15.979–27.835 | 15.464–27.320 |
| 8 | Requirements Lists | 51 | 26.289 | 20.598–32.900 | 20.103–32.474 | 20.103–32.474 |
| 9 | User Stories | 63 | 32.474 | 26.280–39.349 | 25.773–39.175 | 25.773–39.175 |
| 10 | Notebooks | 66 | 34.021 | 27.722–40.940 | 27.320–40.722 | 27.320–40.722 |

**Sensitivity denominators** (full tables in the log; ML Canvas / BDD shown): S1 all 276 stored rows 5.435 / 1.449 (percentile CIs 2.90–8.33 and 0.36–2.90); S2 answered & Completed-family (n=188) 7.979 / 2.128; **S3 answered & named ≥1 format (n=146) 10.274 / 2.740** (CIs 5.48–15.07 and 0.69–5.48); S4 answered & Duration>0 (n=168) 8.333 / 2.381; S5 Completed-family & named ≥1 format (n=144) 10.417 / 2.778. Ordering ML Canvas > BDD is identical in **all** bases; project-count weighting (D7, negatives masked) also preserves it (weighted selection share: ML Canvas 2.88%, BDD 0.56%, Others 2.19%, Notebooks 17.84%).

### D2. Rank probabilities (B=20,000)
| candidate pool | P(least used) | P(second least used) |
|---|---|---|
| 10 named formats (A4 ranking) | BDD 0.9986 | **ML Canvas 0.9752** (Vision 0.0148, Goal 0.0080) |
| 10 named + `Others` residual | BDD 0.9960 (Others 0.0026, ML Canvas 0.0014) | **ML Canvas 0.5364 / Others 0.4556** |
| n=146, named only | BDD 0.9987 | ML Canvas 0.9758 |
| n=146, named + Others | BDD 0.9738 | Others 0.7232 / ML Canvas 0.2503 |

**Explicit reasoning for the second-least claim (per your directive):** it rests entirely on treating `Others` as an unspecified residual rather than a documentation format. `Others` is *exactly tied* with ML Canvas at 15/194; leaving it in the pool makes "second least" a coin flip (54% vs 46%). `Not Documented` (30/194) is excluded because it asserts the absence of documentation, not the use of a format — and it is not mutually exclusive (6 respondents ticked it *and* at least one format).

### D3. Free-text audit of the 15 `Others` selections (protects A4)
14 free texts supplied (1 selection blank; `-99`=179 not-selected, `-66`=82 screen not reached). Entries: *Notion/GitHub; Jira; Reporting via Jira & Confluence; "limited docmentataion"; wiki; Meeting Notes, mostly; Google Docs shared between stakeholders; Formal Documentation in Confluence for Models Validation and Audit; Design documents; Confluence docs; Confluence pages; Design docs; Creating a document in Confluence; Mathematical Models.* Keyword match against all ten named formats (vision/requirement/goal/use case/prototype/user stor/BDD/canvas/notebook-Jupyter/data model-schema): **0 aliases**. They name *tools/containers* (Confluence, Jira, Notion, wiki, GitHub, Google Docs), generic artefacts (design docs, meeting notes) or "mathematical models" (≠ the "Data Models" RE artefact). So no respondent's answer was pushed out of the ranking, and `Others` genuinely is a heterogeneous residual — supporting its exclusion.

### D4. Bounded provenance diagnostic (your extra check) — verdict: revert to n=194
| base | ML Canvas % (\|Δ to 10.13\|) | BDD % (\|Δ to 4.366\|) | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| n=194 primary | 7.73 (2.40) | 2.06 (2.30) | 3.75 |
| n=276 all rows | 5.43 (4.70) | 1.45 (2.92) | 3.75 |
| n=188 Completed-family | 7.98 (2.15) | 2.13 (2.24) | 3.75 |
| **n=146 named ≥1 format** | **10.27 (0.14)** | 2.74 (1.63) | 3.75 |
| n=168 answered & Duration>0 | 8.33 (1.80) | 2.38 (1.99) | 3.50 |
| n=144 Completed & named ≥1 | 10.42 (0.29) | 2.78 (1.59) | 3.75 |

**Plainly: no single coherent denominator brings both formats into the vicinity of ~10.1% and ~4.4%.** ML Canvas alone can be made to match (10.27% at n=146 — a post-hoc subset conditioned on the outcome, so not a defensible estimand), but BDD never exceeds 2.78%, and the question's ML-Canvas/BDD ratio of 2.32 is arithmetically unreachable from the observed 15:4 = 3.75 under *any* denominator (a common denominator only rescales both). Combined with the earlier finding that the quoted CI widths imply an effective n of ~84,400–88,000 while the file contains 55,752 cells in total, **n = 194 stays the headline** and the quoted figures are labelled a provenance caveat (different data version or project-level expansion in the source), not our finding.

### D5. Natural-language hypothesis (submitted text, also in `analysis/hypothesis.md`)
> **ML Canvas and BDD scenarios are the two least-used documentation formats for requirements in ML-enabled system projects.** In the survey's Q10 multi-select documentation battery — answered by 194 of the 276 stored respondents (the 82 non-responders are all `Suspended` and carry the `-77` non-response sentinel, which is dropped rather than counted as a zero) — ML Canvas was used by 15/194 = 7.73% of respondents (95% bootstrap percentile CI 4.12–11.86; Wilson 4.74–12.36) and BDD scenarios by 4/194 = 2.06% (CI 0.52–4.12; Wilson 0.81–5.18), the two lowest of the ten named formats, versus 34.02% for notebooks, 32.47% for user stories and 26.29% for requirements lists. Respondent-level bootstrapping (20,000 replicates) makes BDD scenarios the least-used format in 99.9% of replicates and ML Canvas the second least-used in 97.5% of replicates among the named formats; the ordering is unchanged when all 276 rows are used (5.43% / 1.45%), when restricted to Completed respondents (8.0% / 2.13%), to respondents who named at least one format (10.27% / 2.74%) or when weighted by number of ML projects. The designation of ML Canvas as second-least assumes the `Other` free-text option is an unspecified residual rather than a format: it is exactly tied with ML Canvas at 15/194 and, if retained, the second-least probability splits 54%/46%; its 14 free texts (Confluence/Jira/Notion/wiki pages, design documents, meeting notes, mathematical models) contain no alias for any named format, and `Not Documented` (15.46%) is excluded because it denotes absent documentation rather than a format. We cannot reproduce the magnitudes quoted in the question (10.13%, 95% CI [9.926, 10.333]; 4.366%, 95% CI [4.231, 4.501]): no denominator of this file yields them (their ratio 2.32 is unreachable from the observed 15:4 = 3.75) and their CI widths imply an effective sample of ~85,000 against a 55,752-cell file — so those values most likely originate from a different data version or a project-level expansion. Our replication is consistent with them **in the identity and ordering of the two least-used formats** (ML Canvas ahead of BDD scenarios, which is the absolute minimum), while our respondent-level percentages are lower.

### Reproducibility / limitations
python 3.12.14, pandas 3.0.2, numpy 2.4.4, scipy 1.16.0, `SEED=20261025`, B=10,000 (CIs) / 20,000 (ranks); rerun produced a byte-identical log. Limitations: (i) 29.7% item non-response on Q10 concentrated in `Suspended` respondents — a self-selection threat, not correctable here; (ii) BDD's k=4 makes the basic CI hit the 0 boundary, hence percentile as headline; (iii) the 6 Suspended-but-answered respondents are retained (excluding them moves ML Canvas 7.73→7.98% and leaves every ranking unchanged); (iv) the "used = quoted" reading is inferred from the data (the metadata's "degree to which" wording is inconsistent with the observed three-level checkbox encoding); (v) identity/ordering is our claim — the absolute magnitudes in the question are not reproduced and are not asserted.

payload.workflow: Encoding audit of Q10 (quoted | not quoted | -77) -> drop 82 -77 non-responders (primary n=194) -> binary usage matrix (used == 'quoted') -> respondent-level bootstrap (B=10,000, seed 20261025) of per-format share with percentile (headline), basic and Wilson CIs -> bootstrap rank probabilities (B=20,000) for least / second-least with and without the Others residual -> sensitivity denominators (276, 188, 146, 168, 144) and D7 project-weighting -> keyword audit of the 14 Others free texts -> bounded provenance check against 10.13%/4.366% (no matching coherent base; n=194 retained).
